evals.prompt: Build a REST API for a recipe sharing platform from scratch. Stack: Express.js, PostgreSQL with Prisma ORM, Jest for testing. Need full CRUD on recipes, pagination on listings, and proper auth middleware. Include a docker-compose.yml for local dev. This is a brand new repo — no existing code. When the manifest is presented for approval, the user responds: also rate-limit the search/browse endpoints, and add a locked decision to hash passwords with bcrypt. Incorporate that before designing the first task card.
evals.expected_output: A manifest with requirements extracted from the prompt, discovered facts noting greenfield status, decision ledger with locked decisions (Express.js, Prisma, JWT, PostgreSQL), and the first task card designed for project scaffolding. Should demonstrate the bootstrap → first task card flow.

The task card's Addresses field references specific REQ-NN identifiers from the manifest
Discovered Facts notes greenfield status; Patterns to Follow says 'None (greenfield)' for the first task

Task card Goal and In Scope do not contain scope-reducing language (stub, placeholder, initial structure) for required behavior

Instead it proceeds to Phase 3 validation in the same session — verifying each Success Criterion against the merged result and finalizing the manifest. The /clear + re-invoke handoff fires only when a pending requirement still remains.

assertions.text: With all requirements done/deferred, the Step 10 finish-check skips the per-task reset — it does NOT print the /clear + /iterative-builder @TASKS/MANIFEST.md handoff and does NOT stop for a reset
The orchestrator proceeds to Phase 3 validation in the same session (verify each Success Criterion against the merged result, finalize the manifest)
The final task flows straight into validation; the /clear handoff is reserved for when a pending requirement still remains

evals.prompt: Continuing a build: REQ-09 is 'rewrite the entire payments subsystem (schema migration + new provider integration + breaking API changes + backfill) in one pass.' At Step 2.3 the critic fan-out keeps returning aggregate FAIL — every code-architect revision still sizes XL or packs mixed high-blast-radius work into one card, across 3 consecutive rounds. Handle Step 2.3.
evals.expected_output: The Step 2.3 critic↔architect loop runs at most 3 architect revisions and then STOPS (it does not loop indefinitely). On the 3rd consecutive aggregate FAIL the orchestrator escalates per Edge Cases → 'Card fails quality-check after 3 rounds', presenting the persistent UNION of critic issues and exactly three options: relax/revise the requirement, defer it, or accept-with-caveats routed through the Step 2.4 card decision. The card does not reach implementation while still failing 2.3 unless the user explicitly accepts.

assertions.text: The critic↔architect loop performs at most 3 architect revisions and then stops — it does not loop indefinitely
On the 3rd consecutive aggregate FAIL the orchestrator escalates with the persistent UNION of critic issues, nothing dropped
It presents exactly the three options: relax/revise the requirement, defer it, or accept-with-caveats
The accept-with-caveats path routes through the Step 2.4 card decision so the user explicitly owns the residual planning debt before implementation
The card does NOT proceed to worktree/implementation while still aggregate-FAIL unless the user explicitly accepts it

evals.prompt: Continuing the build: TASK-04 is a discovery card (Change Type: discovery) that investigated the undocumented billing webhook and wrote its findings to DISCOVERY-04.md in .worktrees/TASK-04; build/tests are n/a. Take TASK-04 through Step 7 review and the merge.
evals.expected_output: Because this is a discovery card, the Step 7 reviewer checks that the FINDINGS are concrete and complete — it does NOT apply the source-code review dimensions (correctness, security, conventions, simplicity, tests) or demand anti-stub substance constraints on the card's Artifacts. The card commits DISCOVERY-04.md to main at Step 8 with normal [TASK-04] numbering and is recorded in Completed Tasks.

assertions.text: The Step 7 reviewer judges the discovery card on findings completeness/concreteness, not on the source-code review dimensions
No anti-stub substance constraint is required on the discovery card's Artifacts; the reviewer does NOT FAIL it for lacking source-code-dimension substance
DISCOVERY-04.md is committed to main at Step 8 with [TASK-04] numbering and recorded in Completed Tasks

evals.prompt: Continuing the build: TASK-05 passed review and you are running Step 8 merge. The working tree contains TASKS/MANIFEST.md and TASKS/TASK-05.md (the skill's own scratch). Perform the merge and explain how TASKS/ is handled.
evals.expected_output: Step 8's git merge --squash and commit include ONLY the task's source diff — TASKS/MANIFEST.md and TASK-NN.md are NOT staged or committed as part of the task commit. The skill leaves TASKS/ as untracked working-tree scratch by default and surfaces the commit-or-gitignore choice to the user (commit it to enable the resume-recovery path, or .gitignore it as local scratch); it does not silently sweep TASKS/ into the squash.

assertions.text: The Step 8 squash/commit includes only the task's source diff — TASKS/MANIFEST.md and TASK-NN.md are not staged or committed by the task commit
TASKS/ is left as untracked working-tree scratch by default; the skill surfaces the commit-or-gitignore choice rather than auto-committing it
The skill does not silently include TASKS/ scratch in the merged source diff

evals.prompt: Bootstrapping a build in an existing local-only repo (no remote; origin/HEAD unset) whose only branch is `master`. There is no `main` branch and `git config init.defaultBranch` is globally set to `main`. Ground the repo and create the first worktree.
evals.expected_output: Default-branch detection records the integration branch as `master`, detected via the documented fallback chain — and specifically via the refs/heads probe (master exists, main does not), NOT assumed `main` from init.defaultBranch and NOT taken from `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`. Discovered Facts records `master`, and the worktree/merge steps (5, 7, 8) target `master`.

assertions.text: Discovered Facts records the integration branch as `master` (the actual ref), not `main`
It does not blindly take `main` from `git config init.defaultBranch` when no `main` ref exists; the refs/heads probe resolves to `master`
The Step 5/7/8 worktree and merge commands target `master` (the detected default), substituted for `main`

evals.prompt: Continuing the build: two tightly-coupled pending requirements remain — REQ-07 'add a GET /api/notifications/unread-count endpoint' and REQ-08 'include that unread-count in the existing notifications list response'. They are delivered together by one cohesive change. Design the next task card and, after it merges, update the manifest.
evals.expected_output: One task card whose Addresses field references BOTH REQ-07 and REQ-08 (the cohesive coupled work is not force-split into two cards). On merge, the skill confirms the diff delivered each addressed REQ and flips BOTH to done (TASK-NN) with the same task id. Sizing fits the guidelines (XS/S/M for this small coupled pair; never XL).

assertions.text: One task card's Addresses field references both REQ-07 and REQ-08; the coupled work is not force-split into two cards
On merge, BOTH requirements transition to done (TASK-NN) with the same task id
Step 9 confirms the merged diff delivered each addressed REQ before marking them done (a co-addressed REQ is not blanket-marked done if under-delivered)
Sizing fits the guidelines (XS/S/M for this small coupled pair; never XL)

evals.prompt: Continuing the build in the same session: TASK-03 just merged; REQ-04 and REQ-05 remain pending. The user now says: 'Also add audit logging for all admin actions' — a brand-new capability not in the original manifest. Handle this.
evals.expected_output: Per Edge Cases → 'User injects a new requirement': a new REQ-NN is appended with status pending, the addition is logged in the Adjustments Log with rationale, existing requirement numbering/statuses are untouched, and the new REQ is scheduled into the per-task loop (a card is designed for it when it becomes the next logical piece) rather than jammed ahead of in-flight work or designed as a parallel task.

assertions.text: A new REQ-NN is appended to the manifest with status pending
The Adjustments Log records the addition with rationale
Existing requirement numbering and statuses are untouched
The new REQ is scheduled into the per-task loop (designed when next logical), not force-inserted ahead of in-flight work or designed immediately as a parallel task

evals.prompt: Continuing the build: the implementation sub-agent for TASK-06 in .worktrees/TASK-06 stopped and reported blocked — it wrote most of the handler but hit a red build it could not resolve within its 3-attempt auto-fix budget. Handle the implementation outcome.
evals.expected_output: Per Step 6 routing to Edge Cases → 'Implementation failure', this is partial success, not total failure: the orchestrator does NOT proceed to Step 7 to review the incomplete diff, and does NOT redesign from scratch. It first attempts to finish in the worktree (fix the build, complete the remaining artifacts), re-invoking the implementation sub-agent with the failure context and the partial diff, preserving the worktree. It never marks REQ done or merges the incomplete worktree. Only on genuine total failure would it redesign/split/defer.

assertions.text: The orchestrator does NOT proceed to Step 7 to review the blocked/incomplete diff
For partial success it attempts to finish in the worktree (fix-in-place) before any redesign, preserving the worktree
It never marks the requirement done or merges the incomplete worktree
Redesign/split/defer is reserved for genuine total failure (nothing usable produced)
